answer: Agents deter Sybil attacks via acoustic echo ranging across an offshore reef. A candidate node emits shaped pulses through a spiral transducer toward a surveyed shipwreck relic. Verifiers analyze reflected waveforms to authenticate the node's physical coordinates. Adversaries cannot virtualize nodes because generating valid acoustic responses demands dedicated transducers per identity. However, thermal turbulence around the reef alters sound speed, causing intermittent verification dropouts.
